title: The princess and the pea.
lines: Once upon a time there was a prince who really wanted to marry a real princess.
Not just any princess, but a real, real princess.
He travelled all over the world.
He met lots of princesses.
But there was always something not quite right.
One wasn't kind.
Another never laughed.
And yet another only cared about her crown.
The prince came back to his castle feeling sad.
One evening there was a terrible thunderstorm.
It was pouring with rain.
The lightning flashed.
Flash!
The thunder rumbled.
Boom!
And then there was a knock at the castle gate.
Knock, knock, knock.
The old king went to open the gate himself.
There stood a girl.
She was soaking wet.
Water ran from her hair, over her clothes and into her shoes.
Good evening, she said.
I'm a princess, and I got lost in the storm.
May I sleep here?
A princess?
thought the old queen.
We'll see about that.
She went to the guest bedroom.
She took all the blankets and pillows off the bed.
And at the bottom of the bed she put one little green pea.
Then she put a mattress on top of it.
And another mattress.
And another.
Twenty mattresses!
And on top of the mattresses she put twenty more soft feather quilts.
The bed was so high that the girl had to climb up a ladder.
Sleep well, said the queen with a smile.
The next morning everyone was sitting at breakfast.
The girl came in.
She had dark circles under her eyes, and she was yawning.
How did you sleep?
asked the queen.
Oh, very badly, said the girl.
I hardly slept a wink.
There was something hard in my bed.
I'm black and blue all over!
The queen clapped her hands.
You see!
Only a real princess can feel a tiny pea through twenty mattresses and twenty quilts!
The prince was so happy.
At last he had found a real princess.
And she was very kind too, and very funny.
They laughed together, they walked together in the garden, and later they got married.
And the pea?
It was put in a little glass case, in the castle museum.
If nobody has stolen it, it's still there today.
